# Results — Study 703 (Cypher-Harmonic)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — the
**Cypher** harmonic, the only pattern in the Carney/Oglesbee harmonic-pattern family whose
D point is measured off the **XC** leg (not XA, not AB): a five-point X-A-B-C-D structure
where B retraces XA by **0.382-0.618** (the same shallow band as the Crab), C **overshoots
the original A swing** by **1.13-1.414x of XA** (unlike Gartley/Bat/Crab, where C sits
*between* B and A), and **D retraces the freshly-extended XC leg by exactly 78.6%** —
landing back inside the X-A range, close to X. Believers expect a reversal the moment
price touches D. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the
partial current month is dropped). Basket: SPY, QQQ, AAPL, MSFT, TSLA, NVDA — identical to
siblings [700-bat-harmonic](../../700-bat-harmonic/) and
[701-crab-harmonic](../../701-crab-harmonic/), for apples-to-apples comparison.*

## The protocol

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Pivot detection | percentage-threshold zigzag on daily closes, **pct = 2%**; a pivot is recorded only at its **confirmation bar** (never the earlier, still-unconfirmed extreme) |
| Cypher arm — structural bands (both arms) | AB retraces XA by **0.382-0.618** (the shallow band shared with the Crab); C **overshoots point A** — same direction as XA, `XC/XA` in **1.13-1.414** — unlike every sibling, where C retraces *between* B and A |
| Cypher arm — defining ratio | **D = C − 0.786 × (C − X)**, i.e. D retraces the freshly-extended **XC leg** (not XA, not AB) back toward X by 78.6% — the only D formula in the harmonic zoo referenced off XC |
| Placebo arm | identical structural pivots (same AB/XC bands, same candidate pool), but each candidate's D-retracement *target* is drawn uniformly from [0.30, 0.98], kept ≥ 0.10 clear of 0.786 — "any XC-retracement zone", not specifically the pattern's own 0.786 |
| D-touch scan | forward window of **120 sessions** from C's confirmation bar; first bar whose high-low range brackets D (or closes within 0.75% of it) |
| Execution | enter the fade at the touch bar's **own close** (the touch is observed intrabar via that bar's high-low range — one documented convention, identical in both arms) |
| Base-rate control | ``n`` random entry days per ticker, matched to the **same empirical bullish/bearish mix** as the real Cypher touches, pooled over **20 seeds** — neutralizes the equity-drift confound a directional rule inherits on an upward-drifting tape |
| Bonferroni | pooled headline + 6 per-ticker splits (5-day) = **7 tests**; critical \|*t*\| raised from 2.0 to **2.69** (family-wise α = 0.05, normal approximation) |
| Costs | one round trip = **2 × one-way cost × NAV**; net figures at 5 / 10 bps one-way |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC) *t* of the mean return against 0 (events can cluster in time); Welch *t* for the base-rate and placebo arm-vs-arm comparisons; Wilson interval on hit rate |

No survivorship: six large, currently-listed single names/ETFs, individually named — not a
membership-conditioned panel.

## The headline — Cypher XABC, forward returns at D

Pooled confirmed pivots: **6,055** → Cypher XABC candidates: **153** → D-touches: **127**.

| horizon | n | hit rate | mean (bps/event) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | 127 | 57.5% | +22.89  | +1.08 |
| **5-day (headline)** | **127** | **50.4%** | **+45.77** | **+0.84** |
| 10-day | 127 | 52.0% | +27.69  | +0.34 |

Hit rate (5-day): **50.4%** (Wilson 95% [41.8%, 58.9%]) — a coin flip, dead center on the
interval. The headline mean is *positive* at every horizon but never comes remotely close
to the *t* ≥ 2 bar, and it is not monotone with horizon (peaks at 5 days, fades by 10).

Five of six tickers are individually positive, but **none clears the naive \|*t*\| ≥ 2

## Signal axis — Cypher fade vs a random-day BASE RATE, Bonferroni-corrected

The base rate redraws, per ticker and pooled over 20 seeds, the same number of random
entry days with the same empirical bullish/bearish mix as the real Cypher touches — the
equity-drift confound a directional rule inherits on an upward-drifting tape.

| horizon | Cypher mean (bps) | base-rate mean (bps, n=2,540) | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | +22.89 | −4.78 | +0.99 |
| **5-day (headline)** | **+45.77** | −2.83 | **+0.81** |
| 10-day | +27.69 | −8.35 | +0.43 |

Per-ticker, 5-day, Cypher vs its own matched-mix base rate:

| Ticker | Cypher *n* | Cypher mean (bps) | base-rate mean (bps) | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY  | 21 | −59.62  | −15.57 | −1.06 |
| QQQ  | 18 | +60.34  | +19.17 | +0.51 |
| AAPL | 16 | +128.81 | −29.94 | +1.34 |
| MSFT | 15 | +28.98  | −18.22 | +0.39 |
| TSLA | 26 | +77.68  | −42.76 | +0.79 |
| NVDA | 31 | +47.21  | +47.93 | −0.00 |

**Bonferroni correction across 7 tests** (pooled headline + 6 per-ticker splits, 5-day):
critical |*t*| = **2.69** (family-wise α = 0.05, normal approximation).

- **0 of 7 tests clear even the uncorrected |*t*| ≥ 2 bar.** The best individual reading
  (AAPL, Welch *t* = +1.34) is well short of naive significance, let alone the
  Bonferroni-corrected threshold.
- **0 of 7 survive Bonferroni.** The pooled point estimate is positive and the base rate is
  flat-to-negative, but the gap (Welch *t* = +0.81) is comfortably inside sampling noise
  for a basket this size.

## Tradability axis — the fade timer, net of costs

One round trip = 2 × one-way cost × NAV per event.

| hold | gross mean (bps) | net @ 5 bps (bps) | net @ 10 bps (bps) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | +22.89 (t=+1.08) | +12.89 (t=+0.61) | +2.89 (t=+0.14)  |
| 3-day  | +27.93 (t=+0.72) | +17.93 (t=+0.47) | +7.93 (t=+0.21)  |
| **5-day** | **+45.77 (t=+0.84)** | **+35.77 (t=+0.66)** | **+25.77 (t=+0.47)** |
| 10-day | +27.69 (t=+0.34) | +17.69 (t=+0.22) | +7.69 (t=+0.09)  |
| 20-day | −12.92 (t=−0.12) | −22.92 (t=−0.21) | −32.92 (t=−0.31) |

Every hold length carries the same story: a positive but never-close-to-certified average
that erodes as costs bite and eventually flips negative by 20 days. No horizon is both
profitable and statistically credible; even the gross, cost-free number never approaches
the *t* ≥ 2 bar.

## Third axis (myth-check) — does the precise 0.786 XC retracement beat a placebo?

Identical pivots and structural AB/XC bands; only the D-retracement *target* differs
(Cypher: fixed 0.786; placebo: drawn per-candidate from [0.30, 0.98], excluding a ±0.10
band around 0.786).

| horizon | Cypher mean (bps) | placebo mean (bps) | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | +22.89 | +1.82  | +0.58 |
| **5-day (headline)** | **+45.77** | +86.98 | **−0.52** |
| 10-day | +27.69 | +91.39 | −0.54 |

Placebo candidates: 153 → placebo D-touches: 134.

Per-instrument, 5-day, Cypher vs placebo:

| Ticker | Cypher mean (bps) | placebo mean (bps) | beats placebo? |
|---|--:|--:|:--:|
| SPY  | −59.62  | +29.16  | no |
| QQQ  | +60.34  | +101.24 | no |
| AAPL | +128.81 | −44.18  | **yes** |
| MSFT | +28.98  | +17.81  | **yes** |
| TSLA | +77.68  | +12.86  | **yes** |
| NVDA | +47.21  | +264.03 | no |

Cypher beats the placebo on **3 of 6** tickers — a coin flip — and at the pooled headline
horizon the placebo actually *outperforms* the Cypher's own 0.786 ratio (Welch
*t* = −0.52, not significant either way). The pattern's uniquely-XC-referenced 78.6%
retracement shows no detectable specificity over an arbitrary nearby retracement built from
the identical pivot geometry.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic mean-reverting price index (tunable `mean_rev` knob toward a slow EMA),
pooled across a **synthetic 6-name basket per seed** (mirrors the real pooled sample size);
no network.

| world | *n* (pooled) | mean (bps/event) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| null (`mean_rev = 0`), **20 seeds** | ~36/seed | — | mean **+0.13** (sd 0.86), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 0/20 seeds** |
| planted `mean_rev = 0.12` (seed 703) | 216 | +99.57 | **+5.91** |

The null never fires across 20 independent seeds, and a planted mean-reversion tendency
lights up sharply. The pipeline can find a real Cypher-shaped reversal effect when one is
actually there — the flat, uncertified real-tape result above is the genuine article, not
a broken detector. *(A faithful-engine / power check only; never cited in support of the
real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The Cypher's 5-day fade-at-D return is **+45.77 bps/event, HAC
  *t* = +0.84** — positive but nowhere near certifiable, with a hit rate (50.4%) dead on a
  coin flip. Against the drift-matched base rate the pooled Welch *t* is only +0.81, and
  **0 of 7 Bonferroni-corrected tests** (pooled + 6 per-ticker, critical |*t*| = 2.69)
  survive. The positive point estimate is not robust with horizon (it peaks at 5 days and
  fades by 10) and is not shared consistently across tickers (SPY is individually
  negative).
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Every hold length is weakly positive-to-flat before costs and
  never clears *t* = 2 at any horizon; net of realistic costs the edge shrinks further and
  turns outright negative by 20 days (−12.92 bps gross, −32.92 bps net at 10 bps). There is
  no horizon at which this trade is both profitable and certified.
- **"Does the precise 0.786 XC retracement beat a placebo retracement zone?" — BUSTED.**
  The Cypher arm beats its own placebo control on only 3 of 6 tickers (a coin flip), and at
  the pooled headline horizon the placebo actually does *better* (Welch *t* = −0.52) —
  consistent with siblings [699-butterfly-harmonic](../../699-butterfly-harmonic/),
  [700-bat-harmonic](../../700-bat-harmonic/) and
  [701-crab-harmonic](../../701-crab-harmonic/)'s finding that Fibonacci ratio labels add
  nothing over a randomized control on the same six tapes.
